hero.title: LET'S JUST TRY IT.
hero.body: Shruggie is a small house with two shops: consulting for agencies, and an agency for brands.

why.title: Because not everything has to be that serious.
paragraphs: The name came up when we realised the “marketing industry” as most people know it has to change. With today's tools and the pace of the business, a few people who really know their craft can do what used to take rows of desks. They work properly and quickly, and they care what it achieves.
The shrug is our reminder not to take things more seriously than they need to be. We'd rather try something than think it to death. If it doesn't work, at least we know why.

left.title: What stays at the door.
items: Overthinking, and the structures that grow out of it, where every decision goes through five rounds.
Billing that counts hours and treats the result as an afterthought.
Work you could barely tell apart from what an AI spits out in two minutes.
left.closing: If we make something, you should see the difference.

how.title: We'd rather try one more thing.

cards.label: AS EQUALS
cards.title: Flip the table
cards.body: We like trying new things, and we'll push our clients to try them too. Sometimes that means flipping the table rather than giving it a fresh coat of paint. Either way, we talk as equals, with founders as much as with their teams.

cards.label: AI
cards.title: A better oven
cards.body: AI is a better oven. It doesn't replace the chef. It lets us try and break lots of ideas in seconds instead of following a three-week project plan. And it makes small teams possible, put together around whatever the client needs.

shops.title: Why two?
shops.body: We want doing marketing, and working with agencies, to be fun again. Sometimes we do the work ourselves, as an agency. And sometimes we hand other agencies the recipe so they can cook it themselves.

consulting.label: SHRUGGIE CONSULTING
consulting.title: For agencies that want to run better.
consulting.body: Clean numbers, proper account management and a rhythm that holds. With the Agency Check, workshops and quarterly reviews.

agency.label: SHRUGGIE AGENCY
agency.title: For brands that want to be seen.
agency.body: Brand, recruiting, video, ads and websites, from a tight team that does the work itself.

footer.note: © 2026 Shruggie · Consulting and an agency from Munich.

hero.title: NO 10X. NO OVERNIGHT. JUST A STRAIGHT ANSWER.
hero.body: For independent agencies that often do better work than the big networks but improvise too much behind the scenes. We bring three things from the network world that pay for themselves quickly: clean numbers, proper account management and a steady rhythm. The rest of the bureaucracy we leave out.

stats.caption: Agency-side, from account management to leading client service teams
Client service people led and developed

about.title: We know agencies from the inside. With and without a network.
paragraphs: We spent fifteen years agency-side, in network agencies and independents, from account management to running client service teams. We ran quarterly reviews, caught escalations, defended budgets and saved more than one client relationship that was close to fizzling out.

The main thing we learned: networks keep a tight grip on money and clients, but lose a lot of it to their own bureaucracy. Independent agencies often do the better work but leave money on the table, somewhere between clients, hours and gut feeling. We know both sides, and we have a pretty good idea which parts of the network playbook are worth it for smaller agencies.

rows.label: Best fit
rows.value: Small and mid-sized independent agencies that want to grow without getting too bureaucratic.

rows.label: Not a fit
rows.value: “100 leads in two minutes” theatre, rebrands, pitches.

services.title: Two ways in. One rhythm after.

items.title: The Agency Check
label: Starting point
2–3 weeks
fixed price
items.body: We look at your numbers, your clients and how you work, and above all at which clients actually pay their way. At the end we sit down together and go through a clear plan:
points: What's working and should stay that way. Clients and routines that pay off, even if they're nothing special.
Where money is being lost, and why. Clients who cost more than they bring in, hours that never get billed, or prices that no longer fit.
What happens over the next 90 days and 12 months, with clear priorities and named owners.
gets: profit per client, in plain numbers
which clients carry you and which ones you carry
Keep, Fix, Next and a 90-day plan
items.note: Your numbers stay with us. Happy to sign an NDA before we start.

items.title: Workshops for teams
label: Standalone
half a day
on site or remote
items.body: Half a day with your team, working on your real clients and numbers rather than made-up cases. There are three topics to choose from:
gets: tools the team keeps using afterwards, like the relationship map (Map Your Orbit) or a profit view per client
concrete next steps, worked out on your own cases
points: Client service as a craft. Who really has a say on the client side, handling difficult conversations and presenting your work with confidence.
Agency finances, explained plainly. What a client really brings in, where the hours go and whether your prices still add up.
What AI means for your proposals, pricing, roles and workflows. And where it won't help you at all.

items.title: Quarterly Reviews
label: After the check
ongoing
items.body: The agency check as a regular date: every three months we look at three areas together and decide what comes next.
gets: numbers and goals, updated every quarter
points: Margin, profit per client, cash flow and dependencies, and how they've changed since last quarter.
Utilisation, workflows and the time nobody pays for. And what should change by next quarter.
Which clients, services and people should come next, from the next new client to your first permanent hire.

more.title: Doesn't fit a box?
more.body: A specific problem that doesn't fit any of the three? Then let's just talk about it. Thirty minutes, no slides.

services.body: Founders usually start with the agency check, teams often with a workshop. The quarterly reviews keep things moving after that. Prices depend on the size of your agency and what you need. After a first conversation you get a fixed quote.

steps.title: Numbers and conversations
steps.body: You give us access to revenue, costs and hours for the last twelve months. We talk to you and, if you like, two or three people on the team. Your numbers stay with us, and we're happy to sign an NDA first.

steps.title: Analysis
steps.body: We take a closer look at whatever came up in the first week, using your numbers and how you actually work. It's usually two or three spots where things really get stuck, and they're different for every agency.

steps.title: One meeting, one plan
steps.body: We sit down for two hours, no big presentation, and go through Keep, Fix and Next. After that you know what to do, with or without us.

contact.title: Let's talk.
contact.body: Thirty minutes, no slides. Tell us what's on your mind and we'll tell you honestly whether we can help.

heroAside.text: We only take on a few clients at a time, so you work with us directly, not with a junior team.

items.title: Your biggest client is also your most expensive.
items.body: Revenue's fine, margin isn't. Nobody really knows how many hours go into the account, or whether it still pays.

items.title: The renewal turns into a pitch.
items.body: The work was good, the reports went out on time, and suddenly the client is “looking at options”. It caught everyone off guard because nobody was really looking after the relationship.

items.title: The work is good. Everything else is chaos.
items.body: Priorities shift every day, budgets get guessed rather than set, and anything important still ends up with you.

keepBin.title: What we bring. What stays at the door.

items.title: Financial hygiene
items.text: budgets agreed before the work starts, and numbers you can actually follow every month.

items.title: Account management
items.text: even if your biggest client is the dental practice round the corner. That's usually where the money is.

items.title: A rhythm that holds
items.text: just enough structure that everyone knows what matters right now.

bin.title: Not invited
items: Bureaucracy that keeps your team from the work clients actually pay for.

items.a: Small and mid-sized independent agencies that want to grow without getting bureaucratic. Pitches, rebrands and lead promises aren't something we do.

items.q: How does the Agency Check work?
items.a: It takes two to three weeks. First we look at your numbers and talk to you and, if you like, two or three people on the team. Then we work through it, and at the end we sit down for two hours and go through Keep, Fix and Next.

items.q: What do you need from us?
items.a: Access to revenue, costs and hours for the last twelve months. Plus a few conversations with you and, if you like, people on the team.
They stay with us. We're happy to sign an NDA before we start.

items.q: Do you come to us or is it all remote?
items.a: Either works. We're based in Munich and work across EMEA. Workshops happen on site or remote.

items.q: How many agencies do you work with at once?
items.a: We take on two new engagements a quarter at most, and you work with us directly.
You know what to do and can carry on by yourself. If you want a steady rhythm, the Quarterly Reviews bring us together every three months to look at the numbers and decide what comes next.

intro.title: A tight team for brands that want to be seen.
intro.body: We look after your marketing as if we sat in your office. No rounds of sign-offs and no hand-overs between departments: whoever you talk to does the work. What we tackle gets decided fresh every month, depending on what brings the most right now.

team.title: Your marketing team, without hiring one.
team.body: In most small and mid-sized companies nobody really owns marketing, or someone does it on the side. We take it on: one person you talk to, a plan for every month, and people who do the work themselves.
team.network: Behind that one contact is a network of experienced marketing people. For every task we bring in exactly the ones who do it best, and we work with AI so it gets done faster and better.

steps.title: Getting to know you
steps.body: A short kickoff at a fixed price. We get to know your brand and your customers and make a first plan, often with a quick win along the way.

steps.title: The plan
steps.body: At the start of each month we agree what's next. That might be a video in March, and ads plus a new landing page in April.

steps.title: The work
steps.body: The right people from our network get on with it, with AI as a tool. You have one contact and nothing to coordinate.

steps.title: A short report
steps.body: What we did, what it brought and what comes next. On one page.

price.label: PRICE
price.note: We don't do fixed packages, on purpose. Every company needs something different, so after a first conversation you get a proposal that fits yours. And if you're just comparing prices, we're probably not the right fit. That's fine.

examples.eyebrow: WHAT THE TEAM DOES, FOR EXAMPLE
examples.title: What can be in it.
examples.body: This isn't a fixed list. It's what we do often, and every month we pick whatever brings the most right now.

items.label: BRAND
items.title: Brand and presence
items.body: Positioning, naming, logo and everything a brand needs day to day, so it looks and sounds the same wherever it shows up.

items.label: RECRUITING
items.title: Campaigns for open roles
items.body: An employer presence that feels real, and social recruiting campaigns for roles that are hard to fill.

items.label: SHORT VIDEO
items.title: Video for social media
items.body: Short clips for Instagram, LinkedIn or TikTok, planned so it isn't a scramble every week.

items.label: ADS
items.title: Ads that bring enquiries
items.body: Google and social ads we keep testing and adjusting. The monthly report shows what they brought in.

items.label: WEBSITE
items.title: A website that sells
items.body: New or reworked, with pages that turn visitors into enquiries.

items.label: SYSTEMS
items.title: The tech behind your marketing
items.body: We don't hesitate to build bigger systems either: CRM, automations, dashboards or AI workflows that take work off your team's plate every day.

more.title: Something else entirely?
more.body: A launch, a relaunch, or a project that doesn't run every month? We do those too, as a one-off. Tell us about it.

contact.title: Tell us about your project.
contact.body: A few lines are enough to start. We'll get back to you within one working day and tell you honestly whether we're the right fit.

sections.heading: HOSTING AND SERVER LOG FILES
lines: This site is served via GitHub Pages (GitHub, Inc., 88 Colin P. Kelly Jr. Street, San Francisco, CA 94107, USA). When you access it, technically necessary connection data is processed: IP address, date and time, the file requested, browser type and operating system.

The legal basis is Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR — my legitimate interest in operating the site securely and reliably. Transfer to the USA is based on the EU Standard Contractual Clauses and the EU-US Data Privacy Framework.

sections.heading: VISITOR STATISTICS (CLOUDFLARE WEB ANALYTICS)
lines: To see how many visits this site gets and which pages are read, I use Cloudflare Web Analytics, a service of Cloudflare, Inc., 101 Townsend St., San Francisco, CA 94107, USA.

When you open a page, your browser loads a small script from Cloudflare. It sends the page you opened, the page you came from (referrer), browser and device type, your approximate country and loading times. No cookies are set, nothing is stored in your browser and no profiles are built across visits. According to Cloudflare, your IP address is only used to determine the country and is not stored. I only see aggregated numbers.

The legal basis is Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR. My legitimate interest is measuring the reach of this site in a data-minimising way, without cookies. You can object at any time (Art. 21 GDPR), for example by email or by blocking scripts from static.cloudflareinsights.com in your browser.

A transfer to Cloudflare in the USA cannot be ruled out. Cloudflare, Inc. is certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework, supplemented by the EU Standard Contractual Clauses. Further information: https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/

sections.heading: COOKIES AND LOCAL STORAGE
lines: This site sets no cookies.

If you close the "Prefer English?" note or use it to switch to the English site, that choice is stored locally in your browser (local storage, key "shruggie-lang-hint") so the note doesn't come back on every visit. The entry contains no personal data, is not transmitted to me and can be deleted at any time in your browser settings.

sections.heading: CONTACT FORM AND EMAIL
lines: If you write to me via the contact form, I process your name, email address, message and, if given, company and phone number. If you contact me by email, I process the details in your email. Both are used only to handle your enquiry.

The legal basis is your consent under Art. 6 (1) (a) GDPR (contact form), or Art. 6 (1) (b) GDPR for contract-related enquiries, otherwise Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR. You can withdraw your consent at any time by email.

Enquiries sent via the form are stored in my Client Workspace (Supabase, data centre in Frankfurt, Germany; delivered via Cloudflare in the EU). I am notified of new enquiries by email via Brevo (Sendinblue SAS, Paris). Data processing agreements under Art. 28 GDPR are in place with all of these providers.
Your enquiry is deleted once it has been dealt with and no statutory retention periods apply; if it does not lead to an engagement, at the latest twelve months after our last communication.

sections.heading: FONTS

An informal email to hello@shruggie.consulting is sufficient to exercise these rights.
You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority — in Bavaria, the Bayerisches Landesamt für Datenschutzaufsicht (BayLDA), Promenade 27, 91522 Ansbach.
